articles.title: Mel Brooks Insisted on Shooting His Scenes for Spaceballs: The New One Before the Rest of the Cast
articles.summary: Mel Brooks, the centenarian comedy legend who directed the original Spaceballs, arranged to have his scenes for Spaceballs: The New One shot first to ensure his character Yogurt made it into the movie lest he pass away during production.
body: “We filmed Spaceballs: The New One that Mel Brooks worked with the writers on. He’s a big influence in it. He filmed his part already before we shot. It was his idea: ‘You better film me now because I’m 100.’ So we did,” actress Daphne Zuniga revealed at this past weekend’s 90s Con, according to People.

Zuniga reprises her role as Vespa (now Queen) alongside Bill Pullman as Lone Starr. Lewis Pullman, Bill’s real-life son, plays their child, Prince Starburst. Rick Moranis also returns, reprising his role as Dark Helmet opposite George Wyner as his flunky, Colonel Sandurz.
The sequel’s cast also includes Josh Gad (as Mawg), Keke Palmer (as Destiny), and Anthony Carrigan.

The publicity campaign for the sequel has so far spoofed an 11-film slate for the Spaceballs Cinematic Universe, teased a now-digital Yogurt with ripped abs, and parodied The Force Awakens’ table read photo.

articles.title: It Looks Like GTA 6's Beer Brands Are About to Become Real
articles.summary: It appears that Rockstar may be preparing to sell beer brands from GTA 6 in real life. As spotted by iGrandTheftAuto, labels for three GTA-related beer brands have been approved by the US Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau.
body: These are being produced by a Florida brewery known as Tripping Animals Brewing. For alcohol afficianados, No Mames Vice City lager will have a 6% ABV, while the other two will be 4.2% ABV, which is identical to Bud Light's ABV. With all of that said, we have no idea exactly when or where these beverages will be sold.

They may be exclusive to bars in and around Miami, as Rockstar Games has completely taken over the city with GTA 6 ads. Citizens have spotted various in-universe ads for various GTA brands around the area, and there's also a giant Vice City blimp flying over Florida. The Miami Heat's arena has also been transformed ahead of an unprecedented Vice City-themed NBA game in November.

articles.title: Next-Gen Xbox Could Be $1,800 And Launch In 2028 – Report
articles.summary: A new report sheds more details on Microsoft's plans for new Xbox hardware, including a new handheld device and console, and one of the biggest takeaways is the alleged price.
body: According to Fortune, the Project Helix console could cost between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft opts to subsidize the cost. The system could launch in 2028, the report said.

It's not uncommon for platform-holders to eat some of the cost of a new console and make up the difference with software and services. When the Xbox Series X and S platforms launched in 2020, then-Xbox CEO Phil Spencer said Microsoft was losing as much as $200 on every console it sold.

Part of what might be driving up the price for new consoles is the ongoing AI-fueled memory and component shortages. Microsoft itself is one of the biggest proponents of the build-out of all things AI, so its own efforts are contributing to an environment where the next Xbox could be incredibly expensive. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reacted to this irony, saying it's "wonderful" that GPUs have use beyong gaming.
Additionally, the report said Microsoft might release a "next-generation handheld device" for Xbox by the end of 2027, though there were no details on pricing or anything else.
points: A new report sheds more details on Microsoft's plans for new Xbox hardware, including a new handheld device and console, and one of the biggest takeaways is the alleged price.
According to Fortune, the Project Helix console could cost between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft opts to subsidize the cost.
The system could launch in 2028, the report said.
When the Xbox Series X and S platforms launched in 2020, then-Xbox CEO Phil Spencer said Microsoft was losing as much as $200 on every console it sold.

articles.title: Here Are The Mechanics and Dozens Of New Cards From Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek Set
articles.summary: After a year that featured alternate realities, ninja turtles, superheroes, and hobbits, the final Magic: The Gathering expansion of 2026 is going where no Universes Beyond set has gone before, as Star Trek is scheduled to launch in November.
body: Today, Wizards of the Coast revealed the mechanics players can expect in the set, along with dozens of new cards from both the main set and the preconstructed Commander decks. We also got a glimpse at some of the set's special treatments, including the seven cards that will come signed by the people depicted on the artwork.
Seven new mechanics--two of them found only in the Commander cards--highlight the set, along with a eighth mechanic returning from 2024's Edge of Eternities.

First is Beam Me Up, which allows you to cast certain spells from your graveyard by returning a creature you control to its owner's hand and paying a separate cost. The example card provided is Open Communications, which normally costs a single blue mana, but you can cast it again from your graveyard by returning a creature to its owner's hand and paying two generic and one blue mana.

articles.summary: Sony isn't the only company introducing new upscaling technology to its flagship PlayStation 5, as Microsoft and AMD have announced that FSR 4.1 is coming to more devices--including Xbox Series X|S consoles--in the future.
body: Similar to Sony's hardware-accelerated upscaling solutions for PS5 and PS5 Pro, AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) 4.1 is an advanced, machine-learning-based temporal image upscaling and reconstruction technology that can render a game at a lower resolution and then upscale it to a higher resolution.

While it's highly doubtful that Xbox Series X|S consoles will start offering PS5 Pro-like graphics (both consoles lack dedicated hardware for machine-learning algorithms), this should still give owners a noticeable bump in graphical quality and performance if implemented properly.

articles.title: 20 Best Board Wipes in Magic: The Gathering
articles.summary: While early sweepers simply destroyed everything in sight, decades of card design have led to a fascinating variety of board wipe functionality. Modern alternatives often bypass indestructible keywords and death triggers using non-targeting exile effects or mass toughness penalties like -X/-X.
body: In Magic: The Gathering, board wipes (otherwise known as "sweepers") serve as the ultimate reset button. Whether you’re in a pinch with no creatures while your opponents have full armies, or you’re looking to slow the game down by ridding everyone of lands, these are the types of spells designed to clear multiple cards from the battlefield in a single shot. These kinds of big plays have been a pillar of Magic strategy since the game’s debut in 1993, when Alpha introduced Wrath of God and set the standard for mass destruction. Control and midrange decks rely heavily on these cards to erase an opponent's early momentum, using one card from your hand to level an entire battlefield of threats.

Whether you’re looking to survive a high-stakes 1v1 format or turn the tides in a chaotic four-player Commander pod, having the right sweeper in your deck is crucial. Presented in no particular order, here are 20 of the absolute best board wipes in MTG history, each bringing its own unique brand of devastation to the battlefield.

articles.title: Sony Boss: “Creativity Is For Humans, Not AI”
articles.summary: Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick and Sony Group President and CEO, Hiroki Totoki, commented on the future of gaming today at the Paley International Summit. Naturally, the topic of AI came up, and Totoki believes AI technologies will not replace humans in game development, in part because of the…
body: "Creativity is for humans, not AI,” Totoki said, as reported by IGN. “How to use the technology profile is important. Of course, I encourage my people to use AI in a certain manner, but at [the] same time we try to keep the rights and rights holders and creators and artists.”
For his part, Zelnick said it's his belief that AI itself will not replace a developer, but instead, people who don't embrace AI might be replaced by people who do.

"I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward-looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward-looking," he said.

Zelnick said ideas that are "completely unexpected" don't come from algorithms--they come from creative people making surprising, original choices. To make his point, Zelnick said when he was an executive at Fox, he oversaw the release of Home Alone, a movie that no one expected to be a success.

articles.title: How Dare They Put This Many Parries in a Call of Duty Game
articles.summary: Last night, I started the campaign for Modern Warfare 4, the latest Call of Duty game. I fully expected the usual things one expects from a Call of Duty campaign: shoot some bad guys, hide behind cover, maybe even blow up a tank or parkour through a busy city. What I didn’t expect: Parries.
body: Modern Warfare 4 starts traditionally enough. You play as part of a group of soldiers stationed in Hajin, a fictional city in South Korea. The North Korean regime bombs the city. You shoot some bad guys, hide behind cover, and blow up a giant truck. Then comes the second mission, “Out in the Cold,” which casts you as longtime Modern Warfare protagonist Captain John Price. You’re tasked with infiltrating a Manhattan nightclub and extracting information from a Russian asset. Price intentionally enters the club without any weapons. Almost immediately, a lumbering giant of a bouncer raises a fist, and a string of terror-inducing words splash across the screen.

The boss fight against Makarov commits two grave sins: you need to parry to win, and it’s an instant-fail fight if you miss a single parry. Yes. In a Call of Duty game. Really. I do not want to publicly admit how many times I missed the timing on parry #3. (The fight does, at least, grant you a checkpoint between phases.) It’s a slog, one that completely halts the momentum built up by the action-packed set pieces that precede it.

I fully expected the usual things one expects from a Call of Duty campaign: shoot some bad guys, hide behind cover, maybe even blow up a tank or parkour through a busy city.
You play as part of a group of soldiers stationed in Hajin, a fictional city in South Korea.
Then comes the second mission, “Out in the Cold,” which casts you as longtime Modern Warfare protagonist Captain John Price.

articles.summary: It's no secret that the cost of video game hardware and computer components has been dramatically rising. We also know that the price of the next-generation Xbox console, codenamed Project Helix, is expected to be high.
body: That would obviously make it the most expensive Xbox in history, and a tough sell for a struggling brand. That's twice the current price of a PlayStation 5 Pro, after all.

According to a new report from Fortune, Microsoft is internally projecting the price of Project Helix to cost consumers "between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft decides to subsidize the cost." (Many game console manufacturers eat some of the cost and hope to make a profit on software and subscription sales.) The report also pegs Project Helix's release for sometime before the holidays in 2028, later than previously expected. With component costs constantly in flux, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma warning of increased costs, there's no telling how much Project Helix will ultimately cost.
Microsoft has previously confirmed that Project Helix will play "your Xbox and PC games," meaning it may be expensive for a console but modestly priced for a powerful gaming PC.

articles.title: EA Sports FC 27 gets a PEGI 16 rating in Europe because of loot boxes
articles.summary: European game rating agency PEGI has begun increasing its age ratings for games that contain "paid random items," a process that's seeing games initially rated as low as PEGI 3—suitable for all age groups—bounced directly to PEGI 16.
body: Word of the change came from Connor Hindle, policy manager of the UK's Games Rating Authority. "Since June, newly submitted games have been assessed against an expanded set of criteria within the PEGI rating framework, including new criteria relating to interactive risks," Hindle wrote on LinkedIn (via GamesIndustry ). "As the UK administrator of PEGI, the Games Rating Authority has now begun applying these updated criteria to selected existing digital products."

These changes were announced in March, and are part of PEGI's new "interactive risk categories" that include "purchases of in-game content, paid random items, communication features, and features that incentivise players to continue playing." The new categories reflect the ways we view videogames have changed: While rating systems like PEGI and ESRB were initially created over concerns about violence and sex in videogames, the real dangers turned out to be much more insidious.

articles.summary: Bethesda just gave everyone a solid reason to boot up Fallout 4 again — even if you've already racked up hundreds of hours in the post-apocalyptic RPG and its many expansions. A new release brings back Courtenay Taylor and Brian T. Delaney, the original actors who voiced Fallout 4 's protagonists.
body: You begin the adventure trapped, without any weapons and seemingly poisoned by an active strain of the Forced Evolutionary Virus. Though there are shooting elements, FEVer Dreams switches things up by offering players an escape room-style dungeon full of puzzles. It's a lore-heavy experience that promises to shed light on Fallout's notorious bioweapon. Expect some familiar faces — but with some totally new gear and weapons.

The new campaign is the work of modding group @kinggathcreates, but unlike most fan creations, FEVer Dreams was made in partnership with Bethesda. In fact, the game's description reads, "Presented by Bethesda Game Studios."

articles.title: My favorite indie roguelike action RPG is tempting me to come back with a transformative new update inspired by Diablo seasons
articles.summary: Hell Clock, one of my favorite indie roguelike action RPGs in the last few years, found a way to take the appeal of limited-time Diablo seasons and make them permanent—no FOMO involved.
body: Its "Journeys" work much like Diablo and Path of Exile's seasons/leagues by transforming a normal run through the game with new toys to play with, but they won't disappear after a few months. The newest Journey, the Journey of Miracles, is now freely available for anyone who owns the game.

With the Journey of Miracles toggled on, you'll be able to earn powerful buffs for each run whenever you find a statue and survive the juiced up combat encounters they unleash. Some of these Divine Blessings you can grab are absurdly strong, like one that gives you the benefits of a Shrine (eg, extra movement speed, bonus XP gain, etc) by simply drinking a potion. There's a full list of what each one grants you on the Steam page, and I can tell some of them are designed to enable builds that weren't possible before.

articles.title: The studio behind Life is Strange, Jusant, and Lost Records: Bloom & Rage is desperately struggling to stay afloat
articles.summary: Things seem to have gone from bad to worse for Don't Nod, the developer of the first two Life is Strange games as well as Jusant, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden, Lost Records, and Aphelion.
body: Don't Nod has been struggling since 2024, after both Jusant and Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden, despite being well-received by players and critics, sold " well below expectations." Work on two new games was put on hold and layoffs followed in 2025, but despite achieving "significant milestones" in its restructuring plan, the studio is still in trouble.

"The videogame industry continues to face an exceptionally challenging environment, marked in particular by highly selective access to financing," Don't Nod CEO and Chairman Oskar Guilbert said in a financial update. "In this context, our current cash position does not allow us to adequately secure all the financing requirements associated with our operations and projects."

Thus the opening of the safeguard proceedings, which Guilbert said "is a proactive, protection measure... intended to provide the necessary framework and time to build a sustainable solution, while continuing our operations and preserving the value of our assets, our projects and our expertise."
